mainTopic: Manners and אגדה about Israel's nature; carrying a person in a chair on יום טוב; a בכור that fell into a pit
overview: The גמרא first explains that an earlier teaching was only about good manners. It brings ברייתות on how to eat garlic and onions and how many swallows to take from a cup. It then quotes רמי בר אבא: the border-marking חצובא plant, young trees, and the bitter lupine each stand as a rebuke to people who ignore a clear lesson. The lupine teaching leads to sayings about Israel's bold, strong-willed nature and why the תורה was given to them. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule against carrying meat on a pole on יום טוב. A ברייתא adds that no one may go out carried in a chair. Stories of great rabbis being carried show this is allowed when many people need the person. רבי אמי adds that the chair may not be carried on the shoulders, with exceptions for fear or a pushing crowd. Finally, a new משנה opens about a בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier teaching is only about good manners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the earlier teaching does not set out a prohibition. It only teaches proper manners.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is teaching us proper manners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an earlier question by explaining what that teaching really meant: it is a lesson in good behavior, not a law forbidding something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought the earlier statement set out a real prohibition. The גמרא answers that nothing is forbidden. The statement only teaches the respectful way to act, which is called אורח ארעא.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the way of the land': proper manners and normal good behavior
'It teaches us': the new point the statement is coming to make

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a new law. The גמרא is saying the opposite: no איסור is involved, only good manners.

phrases.english: It is teaching us proper manners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this text, about why the earlier teaching was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the teaching as manners rather than law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the teaching sets out a real prohibition
steps.terutzMaskana: It only teaches the proper, respectful way to behave

steps.title: A ברייתא about eating onions and drinking a cup
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the חכמים teach plain manners. Eat garlic and onions from the leaf end, not the head, and do not drink a cup all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: A person should not eat garlic or onion from its head, but from its leaves. If he does eat it that way, he is a glutton. Similarly, a person should not drink his cup in one gulp. If he does, he is a guzzler.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as an example that the חכמים teach manners even when nothing is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two cases that are only about how a person looks while eating and drinking. Eating from the wrong end, or gulping a whole cup, makes a person look greedy. These are lessons in manners, not laws, so they support the idea of אורח ארעא from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it is taught': introduces a ברייתא as support
A glutton, someone who eats greedily
A guzzler, someone who drinks greedily
All at once, in one go

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שׁוּם וּבָצָל מֵרֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not eat garlic or onion from its head,
phrases.notes: The 'head' is the bulb end where the roots are.

phrases.english: but rather from its leaves.
And if he did eat that way, he is a glutton.
Similarly:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה אָדָם כּוֹסוֹ בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: A person should not drink his cup all at once,
and if he did drink that way, he is a guzzler.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by showing that the חכמים do teach plain manners.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים teach manners that involve no prohibition
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about eating garlic and onions, and about drinking a cup

steps.title: One, two, or three swallows from a cup
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching sets the proper number of swallows: one is greedy, two is good manners, and three is acting too fancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who drinks his cup in one gulp is a guzzler. In two swallows is proper manners. In three swallows is arrogant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching that adds detail to the drinking rule. It says exactly what the right way to drink is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 2 only said what not to do: do not drink all at once. This teaching gives the full picture. Two swallows is correct. Three swallows goes too far the other way, as if the person thinks he is too refined to drink normally.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper manners, the Hebrew form of אורח ארעא
Arrogant people, those with a haughty spirit

steps.whatToRemember: Good manners is the middle path. One gulp looks greedy, three sips look showy, and two swallows is right.

phrases.english: The חכמים taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹתֶה כּוֹסוֹ בְּבַת אַחַת — הֲרֵי זֶה גַּרְגְּרָן,
phrases.english: One who drinks his cup all at once is a guzzler;
in two swallows is proper manners;
in three swallows, he is one of the arrogant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the drinking rule in step 2 by giving the correct number of swallows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two swallows is proper. One swallow is greedy, and three swallows is arrogant.

steps.title: The חצובא plant will punish the wicked
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא teaches that the חצובא plant, which was used to mark field borders, will 'cut off the feet' of the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר אבא said: The חצובא plant cuts off the feet of the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the גמרא was just quoting רמי בר אבא, it adds another of his sayings. This one is a moral lesson, not a הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חצובא was planted to mark the border between fields. Its roots grow straight down and do not spread, so it marks a clear line. People who stepped past that marker and took a neighbor's land had a clear warning, so the marker itself will stand against them.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant (sea squill) whose roots grow straight down; it was used to mark field borders
'Cuts off their feet': a picture of punishment for those who stepped where they should not
The wicked; here, people who steal their neighbor's land

phrases.english: And רמי בר אבא said:
The sea squill cuts off the feet of the wicked.
phrases.notes: It marked field borders. People who crossed it to grab land ignored a clear warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another saying of רמי בר אבא, because he was the one quoted just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The border-marking plant stands as testimony against those who crossed it to steal land.

steps.title: Young trees will punish butchers and those with a נדה
steps.stepSummary: Young trees will 'cut off the feet' of butchers and of men who are with a נדה, because a young tree teaches a person to wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young tree cuts off the feet of butchers and of those who have relations with a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבא continues his saying with a second picture, this time about young trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a tree is planted, a person must wait three years before eating its fruit. That waiting is a lesson for the butcher who rushes to eat meat before skinning the animal. It is also a lesson for the man who does not wait for his wife to become pure again. People who ignore that lesson will be punished, just like those who ignore the border plant.

keyTerms.meaning: A young, newly planted tree
Butchers
Men who have relations with a woman who is a נדה

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רמי בר אבא's pictures teach the same idea. Nature gives a clear lesson (a border, or a time to wait), and people who ignore it will be held responsible.

phrases.english: A young tree
cuts off the feet of butchers
and of those who have relations with a נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רמי בר אבא's saying from step 4 with a second, parallel picture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young tree's lesson of waiting stands against those who do not wait: the butcher who eats too soon, and the man who is with a נדה.

steps.title: The lupine will 'cut off the feet' of Israel
steps.stepSummary: The lupine is a rebuke to the Jewish people, and a פסוק listing seven kinds of idol worship is brought as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lupine will 'cut off the feet' of the enemies of Israel (meaning Israel itself). As the פסוק says: 'The children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of ה׳, and served the Baalim, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, Zidon, Moab, Ammon and the Philistines, and they left ה׳ and did not serve Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: Like the earlier plants, the גמרא names one more plant, the lupine, that 'cuts off the feet' of certain people. Here those people are the Jewish people themselves, and a פסוק is brought as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The enemies of Israel' is a polite way of saying Israel, because the גמרא does not want to speak harshly about them directly. The פסוק is quoted in full because the next steps read its extra final words closely.

keyTerms.meaning: Lupine, a very bitter bean that must be cooked many times before it can be eaten
Cuts off their feet, meaning it rebukes or brings punishment on them
The enemies of Israel, a polite way of saying Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'the enemies of Israel' literally. The rebuke is aimed at the Jewish people, and the words are just a softer way to say it.

phrases.english: The lupine will cut off the feet
of the enemies of Israel.
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of saying Israel itself. The גמרא avoids saying something harsh about them directly.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And the children of Israel continued
to do evil in the eyes of ה׳,
and they served the Baalim and the Ashtaroth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת אֱלֹהֵי אֲרָם וְאֶת אֱלֹהֵי צִידוֹן
phrases.english: and the gods of Aram and the gods of Zidon,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵת אֱלֹהֵי מוֹאָב וְאֵת אֱלֹהֵי בְנֵי עַמּוֹן
phrases.english: and the gods of Moab and the gods of the children of Ammon,
and the gods of the Philistines,
and they forsook ה׳ and did not serve Him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרְמוֹסָא — מְקַטַּע רַגְלֵיהוֹן דְּשָׂנְאֵיהוֹן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of plants that 'cut off the feet' of certain people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lupine stands as a rebuke to the Jewish people, based on the פסוק in שופטים.

steps.title: Why does the verse add 'and did not serve Him'?
steps.stepSummary: If they left ה׳, we already know they did not serve Him, so the last words of the פסוק seem extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק says 'they forsook ה׳', don't I already know they did not serve Him? So what does 'and did not serve Him' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the end of the פסוק seems to repeat itself and asks what the extra words teach. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving ה׳ already means not serving Him. Since a פסוק does not waste words, 'and did not serve Him' must be adding a new message.

keyTerms.meaning: From the plain meaning of, by inference from
What does the verse come to teach? Used when words look extra

phrases.english: From what is said, 'and they forsook ה׳',
do I not know that they did not serve Him?!
So what does the verse teach by saying 'and did not serve Him'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּשְׁמַע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיַּעַזְבוּ אֶת ה׳״, אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁלֹּא עֲבָדוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seemingly extra words 'and did not serve Him' come to teach.

steps.title: Not even treated like a lupine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that הקדוש ברוך הוא says His children did not treat Him even like a lupine, which becomes sweet after seven rounds of cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said, 'My children did not treat Me even like this lupine, which people cook seven times and then eat as dessert at the end of a meal.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question. The extra words teach that Israel did not even give ה׳ the patience people give a bitter lupine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lupine is bitter, but after seven cookings it turns sweet. Israel went through seven kinds of idol worship, matching the seven in the פסוק, and still did not 'sweeten' and come back to serve ה׳. That is why the lupine is a rebuke to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Boil, cook in water
The end of the meal, dessert
They did not treat Me (like this)

steps.whatToRemember: The lupine turns sweet after seven cookings, but Israel did not come back to ה׳ even after seven kinds of idol worship. That is why the lupine 'cuts off the feet' of Israel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Even like this lupine,
which people cook seven times,
and eat it as dessert at the end of a meal,
My children did not treat Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra words in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words teach that Israel did not treat ה׳ even like a lupine, which turns sweet after seven cookings.

steps.title: The תורה was given because Israel is bold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר says the תורה was given to Israel because they are bold and strong-willed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: Why was the תורה given to Israel? Because they are bold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new related idea about Israel's stubborn, strong-willed nature. רבי מאיר says this is the reason the תורה was given to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the theme of Israel's stubbornness from the lupine. Their boldness is the very reason they needed the תורה, which works on them and softens them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the name of
Bold, brazen, strong-willed

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
For what reason was the Torah given to Israel?
Because they are bold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from Israel's stubbornness to why the תורה was given to them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה was given to Israel because they are bold.

steps.title: A law of fire for a fiery people
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל reads 'a law of fire for them' to mean Israel is fit to receive a fiery, strong law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'From His right hand, a law of fire for them.' הקדוש ברוך הוא said: These people are fit to be given a law of fire.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא brings a פסוק that matches רבי מאיר's idea. Because of their strong nature, Israel is suited to a strong, fiery תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אש' is read as describing the תורה itself: a powerful, fiery law. That kind of law fits a people with a strong nature.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
A law of fire
Fit, deserving

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'From His right hand, a law of fire for them.'
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: רְאוּיִין הַלָּלוּ שֶׁתִּנָּתֵן לָהֶם דָּת אֵשׁ.
phrases.english: These are fit to be given a law of fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק-based teaching that fits רבי מאיר's idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel is fit to receive a fiery law because of its nature.

steps.title: Another reading: Israel's nature is fire
steps.stepSummary: Some read the פסוק differently: Israel's own nature is like fire, and without the תורה no nation could stand up to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the ways of these people are fire. Had the תורה not been given to Israel, no nation or language could stand against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same teaching. Here the 'fire' describes Israel's nature, not the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the law is fiery. In this version the people are fiery, and the תורה holds them back. Without it, their strength would overpower every other nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Their ways, their nature
Were it not that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In step 10 the תורה is the 'fire'; here Israel's nature is the 'fire' and the תורה calms it.

phrases.english: Some say:
The ways of these people are fire.
For were it not that the Torah was given to Israel,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word 'לֹא' in round brackets; the meaning is 'had the תורה not been given.'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כׇּל אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד בִּפְנֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: no nation or language could stand before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: דָּתֵיהֶם שֶׁל אֵלּוּ — אֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel's nature is fiery, and the תורה restrains them; without it no nation could stand against them.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the three boldest creatures
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's list of the three boldest creatures, with Israel first among the nations, supports the idea that Israel is bold.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: There are three bold ones: Israel among the nations, the dog among animals, and the rooster among birds. Some add the goat among small cattle. Some add the caper bush among trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש's statement matches the idea that Israel is bold. Two other opinions add more items to his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והיינו' means 'this is the same as', linking ריש לקיש to רבי מאיר's teaching. Each item is the boldest in its group, and Israel is the boldest among the nations.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as what was said
Small cattle, like sheep and goats
Caper bush, a hardy, fast-growing plant
Some say

steps.whatToRemember: Israel is naturally bold and strong-willed. The תורה was given to them because of this, and it guides that strength.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
There are three bold ones:
Israel among the nations,
the dog among animals, the rooster among birds.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף עֵז בִּבְהֵמָה דַּקָּה.
phrases.english: And some say: also the goat among small cattle.
And some say: also the caper bush among trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier teachings that Israel is bold by linking them to ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that Israel is naturally bold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's list of the three boldest creatures, with Israel first among the nations.

steps.title: The משנה: meat slaughtered in a field may not be carried home on a pole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that an animal slaughtered in the field on יום טוב may not be brought home on a pole.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered the animal in the field, he may not bring it home on a pole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new line from it to start a new discussion. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying the meat home is allowed on יום טוב, but hanging it on a pole makes it look like ordinary weekday hauling. The rule is about the way you carry, not about whether you may carry at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he slaughtered it
in the field
a pole used for carrying loads

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it in the field
he may not bring it on a pole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about Israel's boldness and goes back to the משנה's laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, meat may not be carried home from the field on a pole, since that looks like weekday work.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists more weekday-style ways of going out
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a blind person may not go out with his cane, a shepherd may not go out with his satchel, and no one may go out carried in a chair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A blind man may not go out with his cane, and a shepherd may not go out with his satchel. And no one may go out in a chair, whether a man or a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more cases like the pole. In each one, the action looks like a normal weekday activity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the pole in the משנה, these actions take away from the honor of יום טוב. The last rule, about the chair, is the one the גמרא will now question.

keyTerms.meaning: a blind person
a stick or cane
a satchel or bag
a chair, here one carried by other people

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A blind person may not go out with his cane,
nor a shepherd with his satchel.
And one may not go out in a chair
phrases.notes: This means sitting in a chair while other people carry it on poles.

phrases.english: both a man and a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין הַסּוֹמֵא יוֹצֵא בְּמַקְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases to the משנה's idea of weekday-style carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blind man with his cane, a shepherd with his satchel, and anyone carried in a chair may not go out on יום טוב.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed an old man to be carried in a litter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ban on chairs, using a report from רבי יעקב בר אידי that רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed an old man to be carried if many people needed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי יעקב בר אידי sent word: There was an old man in our neighborhood who used to go out in his litter. People came and asked רבי יהושע בן לוי, and he said: If many people need him, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can forbid going out in a chair, when רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounds like a total ban on being carried in a chair. Here a great authority allowed exactly that, so the two seem to clash. רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition, "if many need him," will turn out to be the key to the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: is that so? (opens a challenge)
a litter, a carried seat
neighborhood
many people need him

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שָׁלַח רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi send word:
There was an old man in our neighborhood
and he would go out in his litter,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָאוּ וְשָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: and they came and asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: אִם רַבִּים צְרִיכִין לוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: and he said: If many people need him, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Many people needed him to come teach them תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא שָׁלַח רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last rule of the ברייתא, the ban on going out in a chair.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ban on going out in a chair on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed an old man to be carried in a litter, which goes against a total ban.

steps.title: The challenge continues: רב הונא and מר שמואל were carried on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The challenge goes on: the רבנן relied on אחי שקיא, who carried רב הונא between towns, and רב נחמן בר יצחק carried מר שמואל between sun and shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our רבנן relied on what אחי שקיא said: I carried רב הונא from הִינֵי to שִׁילֵי and from שִׁילֵי back to הִינֵי. And רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I carried מר שמואל from the sun to the shade and from the shade to the sun!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more stories of great רבנים being carried on יום טוב, to make the challenge against the ברייתא stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases show that carrying a person in a chair was done in practice, and the רבנן relied on it. Now there are three examples that seem to go against the ברייתא's ban.

keyTerms.meaning: and our רבנן relied
I carried him out
the sun
the shade

phrases.english: And our Rabbis relied
on the words of Achai Shakya, who said:
I carried Rav Huna out
from Hinei to Shilei and from Shilei to Hinei.
And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
I carried Mar Shmuel out
from the sun to the shade and from the shade to the sun!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָמְכוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ עַל דִּבְרֵי אַחַי שָׁקְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge from step 15 against the ברייתא's ban on chairs, with two more cases.
steps.raayaObject: That being carried in a chair on יום טוב is allowed, against the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The stories of אחי שקיא carrying רב הונא and רב נחמן בר יצחק carrying מר שמואל.

steps.title: Answer: it is allowed when many people need the person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that all these cases follow רבי יהושע בן לוי's reason: if many people need the person, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it follows the reason he gave: if many people needed him, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the problem. The ברייתא's ban is the normal rule, and the stories are a special case where many people needed that person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being carried in a chair is still a weekday-style activity, so the ברייתא's ban stays. But רב הונא, מר שמואל and the old man were needed by the public, so an exception was made for them. A regular person who is not needed by the public may not go out this way.

keyTerms.meaning: there, in those cases
like the reason that was given

steps.whatToRemember: No one may be carried in a chair on יום טוב, unless many people need that person. Then it is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not cancel the ברייתא. The ban still applies to everyone. The public's need is only an exception to it.

phrases.english: There, it is according to the reason he stated:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהושע בן לוי, from the old man's story.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ רַבִּים צְרִיכִין לוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: If many people needed him, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 15 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the stories to a special case: the person was needed by the public.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stories seemed to show that being carried in a chair is always allowed, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's ban stays, but it is allowed when many people need the person.

steps.title: רב נחמן sends a question to רבי יעקב בר אידי about the chair
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells חמא בר אדא, the messenger to ארץ ישראל, to take a detour to צור and ask רבי יעקב בר אידי what the rule is for a chair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to חמא בר אדא, the messenger of ציון: When you go up there, take the long way and travel by the Ladder of צור. Go to רבי יעקב בר אידי and ask him: A chair, what is your view about it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן wants a clear answer about going out in a chair on יום טוב, so he sends a question to רבי יעקב בר אידי in ארץ ישראל. This sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב בר אידי is the one who sent the story about the old man, so he is the right person to ask. The question is simply what the rule for a chair is. As the next step shows, he passed away before the question reached him, so the answer comes from רבי זריקא instead.

keyTerms.meaning: the messenger of ציון, who traveled between ארץ ישראל and בבל
go around, take the longer route
the Ladder of צור, a place near the city of צור
ask him
what is your view about it?

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said
to Chama bar Adda, the messenger of Zion:
When you go up there,
take a roundabout route and go by the Ladder of Tyre,

phrases.aramaic: וְזִיל לְגַבֵּי דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
phrases.english: and go to Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi
and ask him:
A chair, what do you say about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְחָמָא בַּר אַדָּא שְׁלִיחַ צִיּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of the chair and asks for רבי יעקב בר אידי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the rule is for going out in a chair on יום טוב, according to רבי יעקב בר אידי.

steps.title: The messenger arrives and asks רבי זריקא about the chair
steps.stepSummary: חמא בר אדא arrives too late to ask רבי יעקב בר אידי, who has passed away, so he asks רבי זריקא what the rule is for a chair.
steps.simpleTranslation: By the time he got there, רבי יעקב בר אידי had passed away. When he went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי זריקא and asked him: What do you hold about a chair?
steps.whatsHappening: The story from step 18 continues: the person חמא בר אדא was sent to ask has died, so he asks the question to רבי זריקא instead. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same one רב נחמן wanted asked: may a person be carried in a chair on יום טוב? Only the person being asked has changed, from רבי יעקב בר אידי to רבי זריקא.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (literally: his soul rested)
Went up (here: went up to ארץ ישראל)
A chair (here: a chair used to carry a person)
What do you (in your place) say about it?

phrases.english: By the time he went there,
phrases.notes: "There" is צור, the detour רב נחמן asked him to take in step 18.

phrases.aramaic: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi had passed away.
When he went up (to Eretz Yisrael),
he found Rabbi Zerika.
He said to him:
A chair, what do you say about it?
phrases.notes: "You" is plural: he is asking what the רבנן of ארץ ישראל hold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the mission from step 18; the question is now asked to a different sage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person may be carried in a chair on יום טוב, and if so, how.

steps.title: רבי אמי: a chair is allowed, but not on the shoulders
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא quotes רבי אמי: carrying a person in a chair is allowed, as long as he is not carried on the shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי אמי said: It is allowed, as long as he is not carried on the shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זריקא answers by quoting רבי אמי: the chair is allowed, but with one condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "provided that" show that the basic permission is assumed. The new point is a limit on how it is done: the chair may not be lifted up onto the bearers' shoulders.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what (he) said
Provided that / as long as
Carried on the shoulders (from כָּתֵף, shoulder)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי is not banning the chair. The chair is allowed; only the shoulder-height way of carrying is not.

phrases.english: He said to him,
This is what Rabbi Ami said:
Provided that he is not carried on the shoulders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chair is permitted, provided the person is not carried on the shoulders.

steps.title: What 'not on the shoulders' means: carrying poles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'not on the shoulders' means, and רב יוסף בריה דרבא explains it means on carrying poles (אלונקי).
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'as long as he is not carried on the shoulders' mean? רב יוסף, son of רבא, said: On poles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אמי's condition means, and רב יוסף בריה דרבא defines it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not carrying "on the shoulders" means not using אלונקי, poles that rest on the shoulders of the bearers. Carrying that way puts the chair up high and looks like a weekday activity, so the chair should be held lower, in the hands.

keyTerms.meaning: What (is meant by)?
Carrying poles placed on the shoulders of bearers

phrases.english: What does 'provided that he is not carried on the shoulders' mean?
Rav Yosef, son of Rabba, said:
On carrying poles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the condition stated by רבי אמי in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is meant by 'not carried on the shoulders'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means not on אלונקי, poles carried on the shoulders.

steps.title: Challenge: רב נחמן let ילתא be carried on poles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ban on poles: רב נחמן allowed ילתא to go out on poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב נחמן allowed ילתא to go out on poles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule just learned, that poles are not allowed, using a story about רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף בריה דרבא said carrying on אלונקי is forbidden. Yet רב נחמן himself allowed ילתא to go out on exactly that, so his practice seems to contradict the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (opens a challenge)
Permitted
ילתא, רב נחמן's wife
To go out

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But Rav Naḥman permitted
Yalta to go out on carrying poles!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב נַחְמָן שְׁרָא לַהּ לְיַלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a chair may not be carried on אלונקי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן's practice of allowing ילתא on אלונקי contradicts the ban.

steps.title: Answer: ילתא was different because she was afraid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ילתא was a special case because she was frightened.
steps.simpleTranslation: ילתא is different, because she was afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: ילתא's case was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays: no carrying on poles. ילתא's fear was a special need, so רב נחמן allowed her an exception, and this does not cancel the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different (the case is an exception)
Frightened, afraid
Prefix meaning 'because' or 'who'

phrases.english: Yalta is different,
because she was afraid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's permission shows that poles are allowed for anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Poles are normally forbidden; ילתא was allowed only because of her fear.

steps.title: אמימר and מר זוטרא were carried on shoulders, and why
steps.stepSummary: אמימר and מר זוטרא were carried on shoulders on the שבת of the festival, either because of fear or because of the pushing crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר and מר זוטרא would be carried on the shoulders on the שבת of the festival, because of fear. And some say: because of the pushing of the crowd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how two sages were carried on shoulders, and gives two possible reasons why this was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons are special needs that justify carrying on the shoulders. Fear of falling matches ילתא's exception from step 23. The second reason, דוחקא דצבורא, means the sages feared being pushed and crushed by the large crowd, so it is also a safety concern.

keyTerms.meaning: They were carried on the shoulders
The שבת of the festival (when a big public lecture was given)
Fear
The pushing of the crowd

steps.whatToRemember: A chair on יום טוב is allowed for someone the public needs, but not raised on the shoulders. Shoulder-carrying is allowed only for a special need, such as fear or the danger of a pushing crowd.

phrases.english: Ameimar and Mar Zutra would be carried on the shoulders
on the Shabbat of the festival
phrases.notes: This was the special שבת when the rabbi gave a big public lecture during the festival.

phrases.english: because of fear,
and some say
because of the pushing of the crowd.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא מְכַתְּפִי לְהוּ בְּשַׁבְּתָא דְרִגְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of shoulder-carrying, explained by the same kinds of exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shoulder-carrying was allowed for אמימר and מר זוטרא because of fear, or because of the crowd's pushing.

steps.title: New משנה: a בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: if a בכור falls into a pit on יום טוב, רבי יהודה says an expert goes down and examines it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A firstborn animal that fell into a pit: רבי יהודה says an expert goes down and looks at it,
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב. This opens a new topic, and רבי יהודה's ruling continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be eaten outside the מקדש if it has a blemish, and only an expert can decide that. רבי יהודה lets the expert go down into the pit to check the animal, and his full ruling continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
A firstborn male animal, holy from birth and given to a כהן
A pit or cistern
An expert (here, an expert in judging blemishes)
And he will look / examine

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A firstborn animal that fell into a pit,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
An expert goes down and examines it,
phrases.notes: He checks whether the animal has a blemish. The sentence keeps going in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the chair discussion and opens a new משנה on a different topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: an expert goes down into the pit to examine the בכור (ruling continues).
